## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
Resolves the behavior when MELCloud pushes a firmware update and renders the token expired. This is a more user-friendly solution in the form of a `reauth_step`. When an HTTP 401 (unauthorized) is caught in `async_setup_entry`, the reauthentication steps are now offered.
This saves a lot of people their own debugging and the nasty workaround to delete the integration and add it back in.

issue_context.title: Melcloud integration looses connection, token needs to be renewed very often
issue_context.body:
### The problem

We have this problem since a few weeks now. 
We have 3 HVAC devices connected through Melcloud. When we try to use them via Home Assistant there is no reaction. Clicking on any of the available buttons gives no reaction in the UI. 

Workaround:

1.  Goto settings -> Device & Service (the 2nd one in the list, we have a dutch version so not sure about the actual name).
2.  Click on the Melcloud integration
3.  Try to add a new device by clicking on "add item' ("Item toevoegen" in dutch).
4.  Enter your email & password

You then get an error stating that the account is already connected and that the token has been refreshed.
Now it will work again (for a while).


### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2023.11.2

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Container

### Integration causing the issue

Melcloud

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/melcloud/

### Diagnostics information

Will add diagnostic information when this happens again in the future (probably one or two days).

### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

_No response_

### Additional information

_No response_

- get away from the dependency from the MEL Cloud by using ESP instead of the Mel module (https://github.com/geoffdavis/esphome-mitsubishiheatpump/)

The challenge is that the API key which is provided during the authentication, previously was set to never expire or had a extremely long life time. 

It appears that Mitsu has changed the expiry logic, and the key now needs to be refreshed periodically (although I have not been able to find a pattern yet).  The way the MELcloud integration currently works does not allow for a keep-alive or dynamic refresh of that token.

In short, it will work, for a while, and they you need to re-authenticate again. 

Which technically is best practice, but sucks since the integration is not build to do so.  Hoping the owner will update this soon :)

I added the ability to refresh the expired token: https://github.com/cody82/pymelcloud/commits/refresh-token
Should work without any change in homeassistant if only the public API is used.

Edit: Maybe I was too optimistic, it probably requires changes on the homeassistant side. Looks like HA does not call login when it already has an (expired) token. So that needs to be changed.

review_comments: For this one and next test can we remove the side_effect once we have the form so we can continue and end up with an entry created
From line 374 continue the same test by removing the side-effect and continue the flow so it returns `FlowResultType.CREATE_ENTRY`. This demonstrates the flow can recover from failures

I see your point. In this case it should be a `FlowResultType.ABORT`, whereas an `self.async_abort(reason="reauth_successful")` is being returned at the end.
I've updated the two test cases.
We don't need to check the instance type as the `except` statement above catches only this type.

This can on it's own raise `ConfigEntryNotReady`.

Probably make more sense to capture all exceptions in one place than `ClientResponseError` here and all other in `mel_devices_setup`
The only reason I checked only for `ClientResponseError`, is that it contains the attribute `code`, to check if an 401 was triggered. Surely I can add a `ConfigEntryNotReady` to complete it.
I don't think `mel_devices_setup()` is used elsewhere so in that case I would think all exceptions should be caught here and you can clean it out from `mel_devices_setup()`
Why do we catch `AttributeError`? That should normally never be needed if the design is correct.
